sources.title: Long-term empty homes and second homes: Council tax premiums and exceptions
sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.verified_claim: Council tax premium rules depend on actual vacancy, furnishing, duration and statutory exceptions; no sample parcel is assumed empty.

sources.title: Guidance on the implementation of the council tax premiums on long-term empty homes and second homes
sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.verified_claim: Premium maxima and exception rules are council-tax policy context, not evidence of candidate occupancy or liability.

sources.title: Empty private residential properties
sources.verified_claim: Enfield describes reporting, support and enforcement options for empty homes; inclusion in those programmes is not inferred for parcel_30762.

sources.title: Who has to pay Council Tax?
sources.verified_claim: Enfield publishes its empty-home premium rules but actual charge depends on the exact dwelling's occupancy and exemption history.

sources.title: Empty homes
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth sets tiered premiums and exceptions for empty dwellings; no candidate property is treated as empty without council-tax/property evidence.

sources.title: Taking action on empty and void homes
sources.verified_claim: The borough programme aims to return empty and void homes to use; programme scope does not identify parcel_61522.

sources.title: Quarterly data update
sources.verified_claim: Quarterly counts are aggregate council, housing-association and private stock measures and cannot establish vacancy at an individual candidate.

sources.title: Dwelling stock estimates in England: 2025
sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.verified_claim: Official dwelling-stock estimates include local-authority statistics and vacancy context; 2025 figures are provisional and not parcel-level occupancy evidence.
